subject: How to include INLA graphs in knitr LaTeX output?

messages.author: 461a0c7d7557dffc
messages.subject: How to include INLA graphs in knitr LaTeX output?
parts:
Dear list,

I'm trying to figure out how to include INLA graphs in knitr LaTeX output.

The actual code is not relevant here so I used some exemplary code from tutorials to generate minimal example:

# #################################

\documentclass{article}

\begin{document}

<<c1>>=
library("INLA")

n = 100
z = runif(n)
eta = 1 + 0.1*z
N = 20

p = exp(eta)/(1+exp(eta))
y = rbinom(n,  size = N, prob = p)
r = inla(y ~ 1 + z, 
         data = data.frame(y, z),
         family = "binomial",
         Ntrials = rep(N, n),
        control.family = list(link = "logit"),
        control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE)
        )
@

<<c2, fig.width=".25\\linewidth" >>=
plot(r, single=TRUE)
@

\end{document}

# #################################


The code runs smoothly and pdf report is produced. However - it does not include graphics.

I posted a question on SO and solution suggested there was to use 

noop <- function(...) NULL
assignInNamespace("inla.dev.new", noop, ns="INLA")

That trick includes the graphs but again - breaks some functionality of the knitr package.

Is there any method to overcome this problem?

this, please let us know ;-)

Havard,

I posted the same question on SE website. Yihui Xie (developer of knitr package) suggested in the comments that:

I recommend you to contact the package author to remove the function inla.dev.new. I do not think it makes sense: when in or not in RStudio, R will always automatically open a new device if a new plot comes -- there is no need to call dev.new() manually as the author did.

I'm still trying to get some better integration of INLA results with knitr using your exemplary code but still cannot use the full functionality of the package.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to include INLA graphs in knitr LaTeX output?
parts:
Hi,

dev.new() is needed whenever one needs multiple plots visible at the same time, which is not at all an unreasonable thing to want. Yes, a new virtual "device" will be open automatically without it, but it will replace the existing plot.  inla.dev.new() is a workaround for the (in my opinion severly misguided) behaviour of RStudio that only allows a single "physical" device to be available.  While it would be nice to have an option in the plot(inla.result) to specify what behaviour the user wants, a cleaner method is to specifically plot each desired plot explicitly instead of relying on the "plot everything in a rudimentary way" behaviour of the simple plot command (for complex models; a _lot_ of figures are generated!).

Håvard may have other opinions and/or solutions...

Finn L

> Thank you very much for prompt feedback. Much clearer now. I'll try to

I think the issue is that plot(<result>) should give something that make
sense for the user when used in an interactive environment (with R or
RStudio), while plot(<result>, knitr=TRUE) (or some option), should
give output that make sense when use within 'knitr' environment.

As said, we're open do any require changes for this to run smooth,
somebody just have to tell us what to do, or provide wishlist of how
this should/could work.
